newsitem.title: USA: Equitable unit wins $150 mln contract.
newsitem.headline: Equitable unit wins $150 mln contract.

text.p: Equitable Resources Inc said on Tuesday that its ERI Services unit won an energy savings performance contract valued at $150 million from the U.S. Department of Energy.
ERI is among five companies selected from 21 bidders for a project that will total $750 million, Equitable said.

Under the new contracts, energy service companies like ERI will install energy-saving technologies and equipment in federal buildings at no upfront cost to the government. In return, the companies will receive, for a designated number of years, a percentage of the energy savings that are realized.
ERI Services recently was awarded a similar order valued at $100 million for energy performance contracting by the Army Corps of Engineers for four southeastern states, the company said.
"The overall effect of such programs, in addition to saving taxpayers' money, will be to increase the demand for these technologies in other sectors," said ERI president Frederick Abrew.
Over the next two years the federal government expects to award an additional $6.5 billion in energy performance contracts, the company said.

ERI Services, the newest of three primary business segments within the parent company Equitable Resources, delivers customized energy solutions to businesses seeking to improve their total energy efficiency.
